note: Measured against the live stack at MEDIA_PROCESSING_WORKERS=16, UPLOAD_DURABILITY_WORKERS=8.
why_the_plans_efficiency_rule_does_not_a: The rule assumes serial-vs-parallel measures SERVER worker scaling. It does not.
Both runs ran against the same 16 media workers; only the OFFERED LOAD rate differed.
So the ratio measures client transport concurrency, not worker scaling, and the
0.3/0.6 thresholds cannot be applied to it. Reported both numbers separately instead.
what_was_actually_learned: Transport scales 5.5x from 16x concurrency: partially I/O-bound, efficiency 0.34.
Peak processing hit 16 of 16 workers with 64 items pending, so the workers were
fully saturated and the queue absorbed the backlog and drained it cleanly.
Publication capacity is ~1.5 items/s at 16 workers under saturation.
The I/O-bound hypothesis is only PARTIALLY confirmed: the mount sustained 167 MB/s,
which is not the wall the design feared, and the workers saturated before it did.

decision.reason: Workers saturated at 16/16 with a backlog, so they are the active constraint rather than the mount; but the owner capped this at 16 cores and the box is shared. Not reducing to 8: the measured saturation shows 16 are all doing work.

projection_for_the_wedding_stage.expected_backlog: bounded - arrivals are slower than publication, so the queue should not grow without limit
projection_for_the_wedding_stage.projected_drain_note: Even a pathological 500-item residual backlog drains in ~5.5 min at 1.515 items/s.
